heading: Arrest and pre-trial detention (September 2023)
body:
On Saturday, September 2, 2023, a Kyiv court ordered Kolomoisky held for 60 days in pre-trial detention while authorities investigated fraud charges against him, according to Ukrinform and other state media.[n] CNN described him as one of Ukraine's most powerful oligarchs and a key supporter of President [[volodymyr-zelensky|Volodymyr Zelensky]]'s 2019 presidential campaign, whose media and banking businesses had made him one of the richest men in the country.[n] The report noted that the U.S. [[state-department|State Department]] had previously accused him of using his "political influence and power for personal benefit" and had sanctioned him in March 2021 over alleged "corrupt acts that undermined rule of law and the Ukrainian public's faith in their government's democratic institutions and public processes."[n]

[[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] commentator [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] speculated that the case might peel back layers leading to the "REAL backers" of Kolomoisky and his operations stretching back to around 2014, when he said certain U.S. intelligence agencies became highly active in the region.[n] He tied the development to questions about whether [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s "perfect phone call" with Zelensky carried more significance than researchers had assumed, and whether the Deep State had already lost one of its prized puppets.[n]

heading: Kolomoisky arrest and "proxy state" commentary (September 2023)
body: Coverage of the September 2023 arrest of Ukrainian oligarch [[ihor-kolomoisky|Ihor Kolomoisky]] identified him as a key backer of Zelensky's 2019 presidential campaign, a Kyiv court having ordered him into 60 days of pre-trial detention pending a fraud investigation.[n] Writing in the [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] news brief, [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] argued that "Zelensky is a puppet, and Ukraine is a proxy state ... but whose?", raising the possibility that [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s "perfect phone call" with the Ukrainian president was more consequential than most researchers had allowed themselves to believe.[n]

heading: Sanctions on Ihor Kolomoisky
body: The State Department sanctioned Ukrainian oligarch [[ihor-kolomoisky|Ihor Kolomoisky]] in March 2021 over his alleged involvement in "corrupt acts that undermined rule of law and the Ukrainian public's faith in their government's democratic institutions and public processes," having previously accused him of using his "political influence and power for personal benefit."[n] The designation resurfaced in reporting on his September 2023 arrest and pre-trial detention in Kyiv on fraud charges.[n]

heading: USVI disclosure of $1 billion in suspicious Epstein transfers (September 2023)
body: In September 2023 the [[us-virgin-islands|U.S. Virgin Islands]] told a federal court in Manhattan that JPMorgan had flagged more than $1 billion in suspicious transactions linked to [[jeffrey-epstein|Jeffrey Epstein]] and reported them to the U.S. government, a disclosure made in a 2019 filing to the U.S. Department of the Treasury after Epstein died in a Manhattan jail cell a month following his sex-trafficking arrest.[n] Bloomberg noted it was the first time the sheer volume of Epstein's financial activity at the bank over a 16-year period had been disclosed; Epstein had banked there from the late 1990s until 2013, when the firm cut ties.[n] USVI attorney Mimi Liu said "JPMorgan was a full-service bank for Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking."[n] The bank denied letting Epstein's activities slide and said it reported around 150 cash transactions to a federal regulator between 2002 and 2013; the territory had told the judge a month earlier that the bank facilitated over $1.1 million in payments from Epstein to "girls or women," many with Eastern European surnames.[n] [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] observed that the name most associated with elite child trafficking could not surface without a major financial institution attached to it, adding: "Drip. Drip. Flood."[n]

heading: $1 billion in suspicious JPMorgan transfers disclosed (September 2023)
body: In early September 2023, the [[us-virgin-islands|U.S. Virgin Islands]] disclosed in its lawsuit against [[jpmorgan-chase|JPMorgan]] that the bank had flagged over $1 billion in suspicious transactions linked to Epstein and reported them to the U.S. government in a 2019 filing to the Treasury Department, made after his death in a Manhattan jail cell a month after his arrest on sex-trafficking charges.[n] Epstein banked with the firm from the late 1990s through 2013, and the disclosure marked the first time the volume of his financial activity there across a 16-year period had been made public.[n] USVI attorney Mimi Liu argued that "JPMorgan was a full-service bank for Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking," while the territory had separately said the bank facilitated more than $1.1 million in payments from Epstein to "girls or women," many with Eastern European surnames.[n] Epstein notoriously trafficked some of his victims to a private island in the USVI.[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] writer [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] described crimes-against-children narratives as the "darkest path" in the information war and urged readers not to lose sight of them amid political scandal and cultural warfare.[n]

heading: Litigation against JPMorgan (September 2023)
body: In its lawsuit against [[jpmorgan-chase|JPMorgan]], the U.S. Virgin Islands claimed in September 2023 that the bank had flagged over $1 billion in suspicious transactions tied to [[jeffrey-epstein|Jeffrey Epstein]] and reported them to the federal government in a 2019 Treasury filing.[n] Territory attorney Mimi Liu told a federal court in Manhattan that "JPMorgan was a full-service bank for Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking," arguing that the sum bolstered the territory's allegation that the bank knowingly benefited from Epstein's wrongdoing.[n] Epstein had trafficked some of his victims to a private island in the USVI, and the territory had previously told the judge the bank facilitated over $1.1 million in payments from him to "girls or women," many with Eastern European surnames.[n]

heading: Sweden vindication and the Orban endorsement exchange (September 2023)
body:
When Sweden's government introduced a mandatory requirement for public institutions to report illegal immigrants in September 2023, commentators framed the move as vindication of Trump's February 2017 rally remarks — "You look at what's happening last night in Sweden" and "They're having problems like they never thought possible" — which media outlets at the time claimed referred to a nonexistent terrorism incident but which followed a Fox News report on a documentary about violent immigrants.[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] writer [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] argued the headline should have read "Trump was right AGAIN," holding up [[sweden|Sweden]] as evidence that the [[nordic-model|Nordic Model]] and globalism had failed everyone except global elites.[n]

The same weekend, Hungarian Prime Minister [[viktor-orban|Viktor Orban]] endorsed Trump's 2024 candidacy during an appearance on [[tucker-carlson|Tucker Carlson]]'s show on X, saying reelecting Trump was "the only way out" of the Russia-Ukraine war and that "Trump is the man who can save the Western world."[n] Trump shared a graphic of Orban and the quote on Truth Social late that Friday and by Saturday offered an endorsement of Orban in return.[n]

heading: Mandatory reporting of illegal immigrants (September 2023)
body:
In early September 2023, Sweden's government introduced a mandatory requirement for public institutions to report people in the country illegally, a crackdown that followed years of large-scale migration.[n] Commentary framed the shift as belated vindication of [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]], who had drawn ridicule in February 2017 for warning that Sweden was "having problems like they never thought possible."[n] Alongside the reporting requirements, the center-right government — supported by the Sweden Democrats — planned to extend biometric screening, including fingerprinting and facial recognition, to strengthen checks on people already living in the country.[n]

[[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] argued that Sweden had gone from a showcase of the [[nordic-model|Nordic Model]] and the open society to "a cautionary tale for the impact of open borders," and warned that the biometric remedies arriving simultaneously with official acknowledgment of the problem pointed toward a "slow and ongoing descent into digital slavery."[n]

heading: Comparison to the 2023 Florida neo-Nazi march
body: After a masked neo-Nazi demonstration in Florida in September 2023, [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] writer [[ryan-delarme|Ryan DeLarme]] wrote that the marchers displayed "the very same middle aged fedbois with the signature ski masks and NASCAR-Dad sunglasses as made popular by the Patriot Front," and suggested that the group behind that rally, [[blood-tribe|Blood Tribe]], was another "glowingly" obvious front for a federal agency running COINTELPRO-style operations.[n]

heading: Kent McLellan and the "find the fed" controversy (September 2023)
body: Following a neo-Nazi march in Florida in September 2023, journalist [[laura-loomer|Laura Loomer]] reported that one of the few unmasked participants, [[kent-mclellan|Kent "Boneface" McLellan]], had been arrested by the FBI in Florida in May 2012 for domestic terrorism, with the bureau saying he and others were "preparing a terrorist act against national minorities in Florida."[n] Loomer argued that McLellan's subsequent travel to Ukraine to fight with [[right-sector|Right Sector]] and his return to the Florida far-right scene would have been impossible "unless you are some type of FBI or CIA informant."[n]

heading: Allegations of ties to Ukrainian nationalist formations (2023)
body: In September 2023, [[laura-loomer|Laura Loomer]] described Ukraine's [[right-sector|Right Sector]] as "a creation of the CIA" while alleging that Florida neo-Nazi [[kent-mclellan|Kent "Boneface" McLellan]] joined the group in 2014 after an FBI domestic-terrorism arrest, and suggested he could only have done so as an [[fbi|FBI]] or CIA informant.[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] contributor [[ryan-delarme|Ryan DeLarme]] echoed the claim, writing that most genuine neo-Nazis were "in Ukraine where CIA-created proxy armies are training them to kill and our tax dollars are ensuring that they stay armed."[n] Separately, [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] linked the arrest of Ukrainian oligarch [[ihor-kolomoisky|Ihor Kolomoisky]] to U.S. intelligence activity in the region dating to around 2014, remarking that "it's a great year for the clowns."[n]

heading: Endorsement exchange with Trump (September 2023)
body: Appearing on [[tucker-carlson|Tucker Carlson]]'s show on X in early September 2023, Orban endorsed [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s 2024 presidential bid, saying that reelecting him was "the only way out" of the war between Russia and Ukraine and declaring: "Call back Trump. Trump is the man who can save the Western world."[n] Trump shared a graphic of Orban with the quote on Truth Social late that Friday and by Saturday reciprocated with an endorsement of the Hungarian prime minister.[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] writer [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] read the sequence — Carlson speaking in Hungary on sovereignty, Orban warning against Russophobia, and Trump amplifying the "Peacemaker" message — as "narrative convergence," summarizing it as "Coordination = Control."[n]

heading: Orban interview on X (September 2023)
body: In early September 2023, Hungarian Prime Minister [[viktor-orban|Viktor Orban]] appeared on Carlson's show on X, formerly Twitter, to endorse [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s 2024 campaign and argue that a Trump return was "the only way out" of the Russia-Ukraine war.[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] commentator [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] placed the interview alongside Carlson's own speech in Hungary extolling sovereignty and criticizing Marxist trends in the United States and the EU, describing the sequence as coordinated narrative convergence.[n]

heading: Russian military cooperation talks (September 2023)
body: A Russian delegation led by Deputy Defence Minister [[yunus-bek-yevkurov|Yunus-Bek Yevkurov]] travelled to Burkina Faso in late August 2023 to meet the country's military leader, [[ibrahim-traore|Ibrahim Traoré]], and discuss possible military cooperation, the Burkinabè presidency announced.[n] According to Ouagadougou, the meeting followed talks between Traoré and Russian President [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa summit in St. Petersburg in July 2023, and addressed "areas of cooperation that mainly concern the military sphere, including the training of Burkinabe cadet officers and officers at all levels, including pilots in Russia."[n] Ties with Moscow had deepened since the September 2022 coup that brought Traoré to power against Lieutenant Colonel [[paul-henri-sandaogo-damiba|Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba]], who had himself ousted President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré in January of that year.[n] [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] framed the visit as part of a Russian sweep through the Sahel — Bamako, then Ouagadougou, then Bangui in the [[central-african-republic|Central African Republic]] — as Western credibility in West Africa eroded.[n]

heading: Talks with the Russian delegation (September 2023)
body: In late August 2023, Traoré received a Russian delegation led by Deputy Defence Minister [[yunus-bek-yevkurov|Yunus-Bek Yevkurov]] in Ouagadougou to discuss possible military cooperation, in a meeting the [[burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]] presidency described as a follow-up to his talks with [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] at the Russia-Africa summit in St. Petersburg in July.[n] The agenda covered military-sphere cooperation including the training of Burkinabè cadet officers and officers at all levels, pilots among them, in Russia.[n] Traoré had taken power in a September 2022 coup against Lieutenant Colonel [[paul-henri-sandaogo-damiba|Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba]], and relations with Moscow deepened thereafter.[n]

heading: Overthrow and the Russian pivot
body: Damiba, who had led a military uprising against President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré in January 2022, was himself ousted in the September 2022 coup led by [[ibrahim-traore|Ibrahim Traoré]].[n] Coverage of the September 2023 Russian military delegation to [[burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]] cited that sequence of coups as the point from which ties between Ouagadougou and Moscow began to deepen.[n]

heading: Russia-Africa outreach in the Sahel (2023)
body: Following the Russia-Africa summit in St. Petersburg in July 2023, at which Putin held talks with [[burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]]'s leader [[ibrahim-traore|Ibrahim Traoré]], a Russian delegation headed by Deputy Defence Minister [[yunus-bek-yevkurov|Yunus-Bek Yevkurov]] visited Ouagadougou to pursue military cooperation, including training Burkinabè officers and pilots in Russia.[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] described the trip as one stop in a wider push — through Bamako in [[mali|Mali]] and on to Bangui in the [[central-african-republic|Central African Republic]] — that gave Russia a belt of influence stretching across Africa from the Indian Ocean to the Atlantic as Western, and particularly French, credibility eroded.[n]

heading: Sahel tour alongside the Russian defence delegation (2023)
body: In late August 2023, before the Russian delegation's meeting with [[ibrahim-traore|Ibrahim Traoré]] in Ouagadougou, the group — described by [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] as headlined by Wagner — was in the Malian capital Bamako, where Reuters reported that Wagner militants were helping the army fight Islamist militants.[n] The delegation subsequently landed in Bangui in the [[central-african-republic|Central African Republic]], a visit widely speculated to also concern military cooperation.[n]

heading: Russian delegation in Bamako (2023)
body: Ahead of the Russian defence delegation's visit to [[burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]] in late August 2023, the group — headlined by the [[wagner-group|Wagner Group]] — was in the Malian capital Bamako, where Reuters reported Wagner militants were assisting the army against Islamist militants.[n] Mali had fallen to a coup in August 2020, when a group of Malian colonels ousted President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta following anti-government protests, corruption allegations and contested legislative elections.[n]

heading: Russian delegation visit to Bangui (September 2023)
body: After stops in Bamako and Ouagadougou, the Russian delegation touring the Sahel landed in Bangui on Friday, September 1, 2023; the purpose of the visit was not immediately clear, though speculation that it also concerned military cooperation was widespread.[n] [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] characterized the sequence as evidence that Russian influence in Africa now formed a land bridge across the continent from the Indian Ocean to the Atlantic, while Western nations led by France faced consequences for "decades of exploitation and modernized colonialism."[n]

heading: The 2023 "Mudpocalypse"
body: Over the Labor Day weekend of September 2–3, 2023, heavy rain turned the Black Rock playa to mud and trapped roughly 73,000 attendees in what ZeroHedge called a "toxic" Nevada lake bed, an episode dubbed the "Mudpocalypse."[n] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] writer [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] declined to write a full commentary, saying the memes made themselves and that it was "okay to poke fun at 73,000 trendy intellectuals constantly bloviating about the dangers of Climate Change trapped in a mug pit due to a fundamental lack of understanding of how the world works."[n]

heading: Identification of a Florida neo-Nazi marcher (September 2023)
body: After a masked neo-Nazi rally in Florida in September 2023, Loomer publicly identified one of the few unmasked participants as [[kent-mclellan|Kent "Boneface" McLellan]], reporting that he had been arrested by the [[fbi|FBI]] in May 2012 for domestic terrorism, fled to Ukraine in 2014 to join [[right-sector|Right Sector]] — which she called "a creation of the [[cia|CIA]]" — returned in 2022 and was reportedly deported.[n] She said the marchers on Interstate 4 waved swastika flags, professed support for [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]], and shouted slurs at her because she is Jewish, and argued that McLellan's record made informant status the only plausible explanation.[n]

heading: Florida neo-Nazi march commentary (September 2023)
body: After a [[blood-tribe|Blood Tribe]] neo-Nazi demonstration in Florida in September 2023, [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] writer [[ryan-delarme|Ryan DeLarme]] mocked progressive commentators who, in his account, sincerely believed the marchers were personal friends of DeSantis preparing a long-planned purge of nonwhites, calling the belief a product of "comic book minds" clinging to a cartoonish narrative.[n]
